title: PankPall: Communication preferences regarding palliative care among patients with pancreatic cancer
summary:
Background and Goal: Patients with advanced pancreatic cancer often face severe physical and emotional symptom burdens. Early integration of palliative care has been shown to significantly improve quality of life. However, in clinical practice, this topic is frequently introduced too late—partly because the term "palliative care" triggers anxiety or misunderstandings (such as being equated exclusively with the immediate dying phase). This study aims to investigate how patients perceive the term and how, when, and by whom they prefer to be approached regarding palliative care.

Procedure: The study consists of three consecutive phases:

In-depth, semi-structured interviews will be conducted with approximately 12 to 15 patients to explore their needs, preferences, and communication barriers.

The findings will be discussed in a mini-focus group comprising patients, patient advocates, and healthcare professionals. Together, they will co-design a short screening question to help medical staff assess a patient's subjective need for palliative care consultation more sensitively.

This newly developed question will be pre-tested in cognitive interviews with 6 additional patients to ensure it is easily understood and well-accepted. A patient advisory board will accompany the entire project.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion Criteria
For patients (Phases 1, 2, and 3):

Histologically confirmed exocrine pancreatic cancer.

Age greater than or equal to 18 years.

Sufficient proficiency in the German language to actively participate in an interview or focus group discussion lasting approximately 30 minutes.

Provision of written informed consent for study participation and audio recording.

For healthcare professionals and patient advocates (Phase 2 only):
5. Employment as a physician or nurse in the fields of oncology, visceral surgery, or palliative care with experience in treating pancreatic cancer patients OR holding an active role in an oncological patient support organization.
Exclusion criteria:
For all potential participants:

Severe cognitive impairment, manifest dementia, or acute psychiatric disorders that preclude informed consent or focused participation in a conversation.

Diagnosed neuroendocrine tumors (NET) of the pancreas (as the study explicitly focuses on exocrine pancreatic cancer).

Acute severe physical instability or end-of-life stage (based on clinical judgment if the burden of a 30-minute interview is deemed too high for the patient).
